name: Courier pretext leading to a request to dial a USSD code
description: A delivery or courier pretext is used to persuade the recipient to dial a short code, silently enabling call forwarding and enabling account takeover. Encoded and retained, but not published: the advisory that substantiates it could not be retrieved.

source_references.document_ref: Advisory TAU_ADV_007 — USSD based call forwarding / account takeover

explanation.plain: You have been asked to dial a short code to resolve a delivery problem. Dialling codes of that kind can quietly forward your calls to someone else, which lets them take over accounts secured by phone verification.
explanation.technical: Parcel pretext with a vague technical action request and a pressure indicator. Held at DRAFT: the sole supporting advisory (I4C TAU_ADV_007) returned a connection reset on both retrieval methods.
explanation.why_confidence_limited: No verified source. The concept is plausible and I4C is a genuine national authority, but plausibility is not evidence — the rule stays out of the published set until the advisory is retrieved (G-01).

provenance.notes: One of seven rules blocked solely by I4C being unreachable. Not disproven — unretrievable. Promotes to APPROVED review the moment the source is obtained (RESEARCH-004 section 4). First encoding used PARCEL_PRETEXT + VAGUE_ACTION_REQUEST + urgency, which the linter correctly rejected as satisfiable by weak indicators alone. The actual discriminator — being asked to dial a code — had no positive indicator in the registry at all, only the benign guard NO_CODE_DIAL_REQUEST. USSD_CODE_DIAL_REQUEST was added and is now required.
